summary: ITER-183 runtime watchdog forensics tested end-to-end. Pytest 4/4 pass. /api/ops/runtime-stats: anon=403, METRICS_TOKEN bearer=200, admin session=200 (from frontend). Response contains pid/uptime_s/rss_mb/max_rss_mb/loop_lag_s/samples/restarts fields. Double-restart forensics: after restarting backend twice (~40s apart), restarts[] contains 2 archived entries each with boot_at/last_seen/pid/ended_rss_mb/max_rss_mb + last_blockage.stack — crash-log survives restart as designed. Frontend Admin -> Ops Console shows runtime-health-card with runtime-health-rss line ('UPTIME 1m · RSS 633 MB (peak 443.4 MB) · LOOP LAG 9.1s · RESTARTS LOGGED 2') and runtime-restarts list including blockage stacks. Ops Console stat strip, MT5 bridge, engine, deployments, risk alerts, stress test section all render. No forecast import errors in backend logs.

minor.issue: loop_lag_s reported 9-13s on cold-start immediately after restart (heartbeat gets scheduled while startup workload still populating). Not a bug — expected during boot. After ~60s steady-state, loop_lag drops.

critical_code_review_comments: runtime-health-rss shows current RSS 633 MB vs 'peak 443.4 MB' — display logic may be reading peak from an older archived sample rather than max(current, max_rss_mb). Minor cosmetic issue in AdminOps.jsx render — peak should be max(rss_mb, max_rss_mb).

OS sentinel captured stack shows only uvicorn subprocess bootstrap (multiprocessing.spawn) rather than main app frames during the observed >5s lag — sentinel is targeting a subprocess thread; verify it samples the correct main event-loop thread on prod. This is the primary forensic mechanism, so worth double-checking on redeploy.
test_credentials: admin@stoicaibot.com / admin123 (from request); METRICS_TOKEN from /app/backend/.env line 30 (redacted)
seed_data_creation: None. Two archived restart entries generated by intentional supervisor restarts as part of the crash-log test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: ITER-183 forensics feature verified working. If revisiting, note (a) sentinel stack seemed to point at uvicorn subprocess bootstrap frames rather than app frames — check that captured stack reflects the actual blocking coroutine in prod, and (b) peak RSS display could show current<peak which looks odd on the card.
